notes: The Cohorts page was a catalog. It listed the peer groups, said how many members each had, and stopped. There was nowhere to go. Member count is not what decides whether a cohort premium means anything — coverage is. A cohort of 503 names whose baseline rests on six modelled members is not a baseline, and the catalog rendered it identically to one with full coverage. The coverage figure was computed and disclosed in the tool output the whole time; the page just never showed it. And "has a model" is itself two different things. A *seeded* model is a mechanical starting point. A *considered* one
